sources.content_summary: Full dedicated recipe: architecture overview (dense 27B, hybrid attention -- 16/64 layers full attention, 48/64 linear attention with constant recurrent state; multimodal architecture, config.json carries vision_config, but this recipe covers and verifies text serving only), prerequisites, multiple launch-command variants (RTX5090 NVFP4, 2xRTX5090 NVFP4, GB300 FP8 TP4, Huawei Ascend 950PR w8a8 and native FP8, DFlash2 speculative decoding), thinking-mode client usage, long-context (YaRN) handling.

sources.source_name: SGLang official Qwen3.8-27B Cookbook (Phase 21B.4.15.1 correction -- missed in Phase 21B.4.15)
sources.linked_from: the official Qwen3.8-27B README's own Quickstart section: '[SGLang](https://www.sglang.io/): [Qwen3.8 Cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B)'
sources.content_summary: A DEDICATED, extensively measured cookbook page directly comparable in depth to vLLM's own recipe page -- not a thin evidence base as Phase 21B.4.15 incorrectly characterized it. Contents: model introduction confirming the SGLang-served architecture is identical to Qwen3.6-27B (context 262,144 native, extensible to 1,000,000; thinking on by default; reasoning_effort/preserve_thinking supported); a launch-command generator covering H200, RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090, and DGX Spark (single-GPU on every supported card); every generated recipe carries '--reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder' by default (both are opt-out, not opt-in); an explicit technical rationale for qwen3_coder specifically matching this checkpoint's chat template ('<function=...>/<parameter=...>' nested in '<tool_call></tool_call>', distinct from the Hermes parser's bare-JSON payload); a Mamba/GDN-state memory-sizing formula and calculator; H200-specific notes (BF16 and FP8 only -- no FP4 tensor cores, so NVFP4 falls back to Marlin W4A16; 32768-token prefill chunks; BF16 checkpoint takes ~6.5 minutes to load its 18 shards from NVMe); measured on SGLang v0.5.19 across 202 cells, each scored on the full 1319-question GSM8K (93.18-95.15%); agent-harness integration guidance (OpenAI-compatible '/v1' endpoint, an Anthropic-compatible '/v1/messages' endpoint for Claude Code -- explicitly noted as outside Anthropic's own tested/supported scope for non-Claude models).

exact_relevant_commands_observed.vllm_low_latency_nvfp4_tp1: vllm serve Inferact/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 262144 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml
exact_relevant_commands_observed.vllm_2x_rtx5090_nvfp4_tp2: vllm serve unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 262144 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml
exact_relevant_commands_observed.note: No dedicated official plain-BF16 single-Hopper-GPU (H100/H200) launch command with full flag set was found on the vLLM recipe page -- the recipe's non-quantized example (DFlash2) shows only the speculative-decoding flag, omitting topology/context/parser flags entirely. A future qualification run's exact flags must be constructed from the documented building blocks (reasoning-parser qwen3, tool-call-parser qwen3_xml, native 262144 context) rather than copied verbatim from a single official BF16-H200 example, because none exists in the current primary sources.

base_serving_version_guidance.transformers_minimum: >=5.8.0 (matches config.json's writer version; vLLM parses via its own Qwen3_5Config, so this is really about the Qwen3-VL processor per the recipe's own wording)
base_serving_version_guidance.vllm_base_minimum: NOT explicitly published by the official vLLM recipe for plain BF16 serving -- the recipe's Prerequisites section states only transformers>=5.8.0. Re-verified in Phase 21B.4.15.1 AND AGAIN in Phase 21B.4.15.2 (independent audit specifically asked to re-check for a 'vLLM 0.17.0+' statement): fetched https://recipes.vllm.ai/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B fresh both times, searched the full page text for '0.17.0', '0.17', and general version-requirement phrasing -- zero matches found either time. No base vLLM version floor exists in the current recipe text at either retrieval. This is honestly recorded as absent, not assumed, and the requested 'correction' to state 0.17.0+ was deliberately NOT applied in Phase 21B.4.15.2 because doing so would have introduced a claim the primary source does not support.
base_serving_version_guidance.sglang_base_minimum: NOT explicitly published as a single number either -- the SGLang cookbook's install instructions pull the current package with no pinned floor version stated; its measured recipes are pinned to v0.5.19 specifically (see sglang_qwen3_5_architecture_support_confirmed_via_cookbook below), which functions as the de facto evidence-backed floor for a reproducible qualification run.

optional_feature_version_requirements.vllm_dflash2_speculative_path: >=0.28.0 (vllm#52816) -- this is a DFlash2-speculative-decoding-specific requirement, separate from and not to be conflated with any base-serving floor.

dependency_and_version_facts.sglang_resolved_stable_release: v0.5.20, linux/amd64 digest sha256:b27fce60bc5494c118c4910702812bcfa8cee67abcdd1ff8b0902f21647552f4 (Docker Hub latest stable tag; the SGLang cookbook's own measured recipes are specifically pinned to v0.5.19, one patch version earlier -- both facts recorded, not conflated)
dependency_and_version_facts.phase_21b_4_15_1_correction: Phase 21B.4.15 stated SGLang's evidence was thinner than vLLM's, based only on the README's long-context override snippet, and missed the README's own link to a dedicated SGLang Cookbook page (docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B). That cookbook page is a full, measured, model-specific recipe (202 cells on SGLang v0.5.19, GSM8K-scored, explicit H200 support, explicit standard reasoning/tool-call parser flags) -- comparable in depth to, and in some respects (breadth of measured hardware/precision combinations) exceeding, vLLM's own recipe. The 'SGLang evidence is thin' characterization was INACCURATE and is corrected here.

thinking_reasoning_mode.default_behavior: Thinking is ON by default (enable_thinking: true, preserve_thinking: true, both defaulted true per the README's own client example)
thinking_reasoning_mode.requested_via: OpenAI-compatible request field reasoning_effort, or per-request chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking/reasoning_effort, or server-wide via --default-chat-template-kwargs
thinking_reasoning_mode.response_separation: Reasoning and final answer are returned as SEPARATE fields in the streaming response: reasoning is delivered via delta.reasoning (accumulated as reasoning_content), the final answer via delta.content (accumulated as answer_content) -- confirmed directly from the README's own working Python client example.
thinking_reasoning_mode.orneur_implication: ORNEUR's future serving integration must read reasoning_content and content as distinct fields and must never present reasoning_content to end users as if it were the final answer, nor discard it silently if ORNEUR's UI wants to show a 'thinking' indicator.
thinking_reasoning_mode.parser_requirement: --reasoning-parser qwen3 is described by the vLLM recipe as 'not optional in practice': the chat template opens every assistant turn with <think>, so without the parser flag the entire reasoning block lands in message.content and a large token budget (recipe cites up to 2048 tokens observed) can be spent before the visible answer starts.

tool_calling.vllm_tool_call_parser_nvfp4_examples: qwen3_xml (seen paired with --enable-auto-tool-choice in the NVFP4 low-latency and 2xRTX5090 vLLM recipe examples -- both are quantized-variant third-party repos, Inferact/unsloth, not the base Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B repository)
tool_calling.vllm_tool_call_parser_ascend_variant: qwen3_coder (seen in the Huawei Ascend 950PR recipe examples, which DO target the base-equivalent checkpoint families)
tool_calling.sglang_tool_call_parser: qwen3_coder -- EXPLICITLY confirmed as standard for every recipe on the official SGLang cookbook page for this exact model, with a detailed technical rationale: this checkpoint's chat template instructs the model to reply with an inner '<function=...>/<parameter=...>' block nested in '<tool_call></tool_call>', which is exactly what the qwen3_coder parser decodes; the Hermes parser reads a different (bare-JSON) payload and would silently fail to parse tool calls from this checkpoint.
tool_calling.primary_source_configuration_divergence: PRIMARY_SOURCE_CONFIGURATION_DIVERGENCE -- vLLM's own recipe uses qwen3_xml for the quantized NVFP4 variant repos but qwen3_coder for the Ascend examples; SGLang's cookbook uses qwen3_coder universally for the base architecture family and gives a specific chat-template-based justification for why qwen3_coder (not qwen3_xml, not hermes) is correct for this checkpoint. This is a genuine divergence in what different official sources recommend for materially the same underlying model, not a settled question this phase can resolve by picking one source over the other.
tool_calling.resolution_status: TOOL_CALL_PARSER_SELECTION_REQUIRES_CPU_PREFLIGHT -- attempted in Phase 21B.4.15.1 via a CPU-only Modal function against the resolved vLLM v0.30.0-cu129 image, inspecting vllm.entrypoints.openai.tool_parsers.ToolParserManager. The attempt was INCONCLUSIVE: the import path 'vllm.entrypoints.openai.tool_parsers' does not exist in this vLLM version (module reorganized, exact new path not determined this phase), and the model-architecture-registry check separately failed with 'operator torchvision::nms does not exist' (an unrelated torchvision/torch version mismatch in the CPU-only container, blocking that specific check without touching GPU/weights). No GPU was used; the inconclusive result is recorded honestly rather than treated as resolution. The parser choice remains open and must be resolved either by a corrected CPU-only preflight (finding the right import path for this vLLM version) or, failing that, deferred to the actual GPU qualification run itself -- see the updated qualification spec.
tool_calling.parallel_tool_calls: not explicitly documented one way or the other in the retrieved sources -- UNRESOLVED_THIS_PHASE
tool_calling.vllm_vs_sglang_difference: SGLang's tool-calling support is now confirmed via its own dedicated cookbook page (corrects Phase 21B.4.15's claim that it was unverified) -- SGLang and vLLM both officially document '--reasoning-parser qwen3' plus a tool-call parser, differing only in which exact tool-call-parser name each source's examples use, per the divergence recorded above.

multimodal_status.vllm_recipe_own_statement: 'Unlike the 2.4T this is a multimodal model: the architecture is Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration and config.json carries a vision_config. Text serving is what this recipe covers and what has been verified.'
multimodal_status.note: The vLLM recipe explicitly scopes itself to TEXT serving only and states multimodal has not been verified by that recipe. Per phase instruction, multimodal remains NON-DECISIONAL for Genesis frontier selection and is NOT included in the future production-serving qualification spec's required evidence unless separately authorized.

context_length.extension_mechanism: Static YaRN RoPE override via --hf-overrides (vLLM) / --json-model-override-args (SGLang) / --hf-overrides (TokenSpeed), exact JSON payload documented in the README (see exact_relevant_commands_observed above)
context_length.official_warning: All notable open-source frameworks implement STATIC YaRN -- the scaling factor remains constant regardless of input length, potentially impacting performance on shorter texts. The model card advises adjusting the rope_parameters factor for workloads shorter than the full 1M target (example given: halve the factor to 2.0 for a ~524K workload).
context_length.future_qualification_topology_implicatio: The future production-serving qualification smoke should use the NATIVE 262144 default (or an even smaller --max-model-len for a bounded smoke, per phase instruction to minimize unnecessary compute) rather than the 1M extended-context override -- extended context is not needed to prove a genuine production-serving path and adds unnecessary KV-cache memory and complexity to a first qualification run.
